land.text: the whole Argentine state of 1929, handed to Cliopatria's Argentine Republic row

predecessors.note: Not a real founding: Cliopatria's 'Argentine Confederation' row (1834-1929) and its 'Argentine Republic' row (1930-2024) are one state on the same land (shapes of 2,792,557 km2 in both 1929 and 1930). The page dates only the coup of 1930.

capitals.name: Buenos Aires
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Buenos Aires 34°36′S 58°23′W'. The page does not date the seat separately.

keyframe_review.note: 2,792,557 km2 against the infobox's 2,780,085 km2 (ratio 1.004; the page gives no year or source for it). The mainland and Tierra del Fuego only: the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the 965,597 km2 Antarctic claim ('Argentina claims 965,597 km2 in Antarctica') are outside it, correctly, since they are claims. The 1930 start is the row boundary, not a new state.

unverified: the page is silent on any frontier change in the 1930s (it records only 'a controversial treaty with the United Kingdom' without a date or territory). Against 1930-1935 the grid exchanges three cells (about 760 km2 each way, 0.03 % of the area): three cells on the Paraguay and Pilcomayo frontier go to Paraguay and three cells north of Formosa, held by Cliopatria's Bolivia shape in 1930, become Argentine. 2,792,291 km2, ratio 1.004 to the infobox. Read as a redraw of the river frontier, not a transfer.

Identical to 1936-2023. The page's claim of sovereignty over 'the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands' is a claim and is not drawn; the 1982 occupation is an occupation event.

region.text: the whole Argentine state, handed over by Cliopatria's Argentine Confederation row

ledger.note: 1930: Cliopatria's Argentine Republic row begins on the same land; one state, not a founding. The page dates the coup that ushered in the era: 'In 1930, Yrigoyen was ousted from power by the military led by José Félix Uriburu', beginning 'the so-called "Infamous Decade" (1930–1943)'. The page gives no month.

region.text: three grid cells (about 760 km2) of the northern Formosa frontier that Cliopatria's 1936 Argentine shape adds; no page names them

ledger.note: 1936: Cliopatria's Argentine shape adds three cells north of Formosa that its 1930 Bolivia shape held. Page silent: no page opened dates or names this change; recorded so that the shape change has an event. Read as a redraw of the river frontier.

region.text: three grid cells (about 760 km2) on the Paraguay and Pilcomayo river frontier that Cliopatria's 1936 Argentine shape drops; no page names them

ledger.note: 1936: Cliopatria's Argentine shape drops three cells on the Paraguay and Pilcomayo frontier to Paraguay. Page silent, as for the gain above; the two exchanges are a redraw of the river frontier.

region.text: the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (the infobox's areas of the war)

ledger.note: 2 April 1982: Argentina invades and occupies the Falkland Islands. 'The conflict began on 2 April 1982 when Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands'; South Georgia followed 'the next day' (Falklands War page) or in March (Argentina page: 'In March 1982, an Argentine force took control of the British territory of South Georgia'). The pages differ on South Georgia's date; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape holds 44 of the 47 Falklands cells in 1982.

region.text: the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (the infobox's areas of the war)

ledger.note: 14 June 1982: the Argentine garrison surrenders at Stanley. 'The conflict lasted 74 days and ended with an Argentine surrender on 14 June, which formally returned possession to Britain.'

wars.name: Falklands War

zones.text: the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (the infobox's areas of the war)

wars.outcome: British victory: Argentina occupied the islands from 2 April and surrendered on 14 June 1982, 'which formally returned possession to Britain'. No border changed; Argentina keeps its claim.
wars.note: Infobox dates '2 April – 14 June 1982'. The Argentina page gives 'on 2 April, Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands' and 'Argentine forces surrendered on 14 June'.

certainty.note: The land frontiers are river and treaty lines ('sharing land borders with Chile across the Andes to the west'); the pages opened give no dated treaty (page silent). The Falklands, South Georgia and the Antarctic sector are claims, not drawn.

sources.title: Argentina
sources.note: Identity, capital, infobox area 2,780,085 km2, the 1930 coup year, the claims, 1982 dates. Silent on the Beagle Channel, the Paraguay frontier and any 1930s border change.

notes: BUDGET: two pages (Argentina; Falklands War). ONE STATE, TWO ROWS: Cliopatria's Argentine Confederation (1834-1929, argentine-confederation dossier, another part) and Argentine Republic (1930-2024) are the same Argentine state on the same land; the 1930 'found' is a row boundary at confidence 1. The colour agent should give both one colour. 1936: the grid swaps three cells with Paraguay (out) and three cells held by Bolivia in 1930 (in); the page is silent, so the two events are confidence 1 and read as a river-frontier redraw. A gap-filler may open 'Argentina-Paraguay border' and 'Gran Chaco'; the bolivia dossier (another part) may carry the Bolivian side. NOT OPENED (budget): the Beagle conflict (1977-1984; no shape change), the Puna de Atacama, Martin Garcia Island, Antarctic claim. COUNTERPART: british-colonial-empire holds the Falklands in Cliopatria's 1982 shape (44 of 47 cells); the eu-11 dossier should carry the matching occupation events. Rulers omitted: no list page opened. Region names: countries 'Falkland Is.' and 'S. Geo. and the Is.' are Natural Earth names in the gazetteer.
